title: Major Sporting Events (Indicia and Images) Protection Bill 2014
short_title: Major Sporting Events (Indicia and Images) Protection Bill 2014

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: This bill stops businesses from using event logos and images without permission for the Asian Cup 2015, Cricket World Cup 2015, and Commonwealth Games 2018.
It gives the Customs CEO power to seize infringing goods at the border, similar to existing trade mark and copyright laws.
The protection ends on 30 June 2015 for the Asian Cup, 31 March 2016 for the Cricket World Cup, and 31 December 2018 for the Commonwealth Games.
changes: The bill bans unauthorised commercial use of protected indicia and images.
It allows the Customs CEO to seize infringing goods at the border.
It exempts use for information, criticism, or review.
It provides remedies like injunctions, damages, corrective advertising, and seizure of goods.
It protects existing contractual agreements between states, territories, and authorising bodies.
summary.affected: Event owners, sponsors, businesses, the public, and the Customs CEO.

speeches.speaker: Laurie Ferguson
speeches.brief: Detailed the committee's sixth report covering 18 bills and 175 legislative instruments, and flagged concerns that the G20 (Safety and Security) Complementary Bill 2014 would roll back Commonwealth law at Brisbane Airport during the November G20 summit without a human rights assessment of the Queensland provisions being applied.

speeches.speaker: Tony Zappia
speeches.brief: Supported the Major Sporting Events bill protecting the 2015 Asian Cup, the 2015 Cricket World Cup and the 2018 Gold Coast Commonwealth Games from ambush marketing, but criticised the budget's $22.8 million cut to the Australian Sports Commission on top of an earlier $17 million cut to sporting communities funding.

speeches.speaker: Steve Irons
speeches.brief: Supported the bill, recalled a 2010 World Cup ambush marketing stunt in which 36 fans wearing a beer brand's colours were removed from a match, and detailed the new Burswood stadium in his electorate, settling under 740,000 tonnes of sand ahead of a contract awarded on 15 April to a consortium led by Brookfield Financial and John Laing.

speeches.speaker: Sharon Claydon
speeches.brief: Backed the bill, credited a $10 million Labor investment for upgrading Newcastle's Hunter Stadium to host Asian Cup matches, described Newcastle's hosting of the Special Olympics Asia Pacific Games with 2,000 competitors from 30 nations, and criticised the budget's nearly $23 million cut to the Australian Sports Commission, including the Active After-school Communities program which had received $39.4 million under Labor.

speeches.speaker: John Alexander
speeches.brief: Supported the bill, noted the Treasurer's budget announcement of $156 million in federal funding for the Gold Coast Commonwealth Games, and cited estimates that global sports tourism is worth $600 billion a year, with sports tourists worth $232 a day to the Australian economy.
